entries.title: Why readings feel so accurate
entries.content: The Barnum (Forer) effect: people rate vague statements like 'you can be hard on yourself' as a perfect fit, especially from a trusted source. In 1949 Forer gave students the same 'personal' profile and they rated it 4.3 out of 5. Use saju as a mirror for reflection, not proof.
entries.source: Forer (1949), Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology; Barnum effect - Wikipedia
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Catch, check, change (reframing)
entries.content: A core tool from cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT): catch the thought, check the evidence for and against it, then change it to something more balanced. Studies link this to fewer anxiety and depression symptoms.
entries.source: APA: What is CBT?; Cognitive Restructuring and Psychotherapy Outcome: A Meta-Analytic Review - PMC
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: CBT for work stress
entries.content: Reviews find CBT skills help with job stress more than general workplace programs. Reframing stressful thoughts helps people feel back in control and lowers burnout.
entries.source: The Efficacy of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy: A Review of Meta-analyses - PMC
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Taming imposter feelings
entries.content: Stress can make one mistake feel like proof you don't belong. Write the thought down, list evidence for and against it, and talk to yourself like you would a coworker.
entries.source: Workbook II: Understanding Cognitive Distortions & Imposter Fears
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Self-compassion, three parts
entries.content: Self-compassion means kindness instead of self-criticism, remembering everyone struggles, and noticing pain without drowning in it. Research links it to less anxiety and more motivation, not less.
entries.source: Neff (2003), Self and Identity; Self-compassion writing RCT
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Write kindly to yourself
entries.content: Writing about a hard event in a kind, accepting way for about 15 minutes improved coping and lowered depression in a randomized trial, more than trying to boost self-esteem.
entries.source: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Self-Compassion Writing Intervention for Adults With Mental Illness
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Short daily practice works
entries.content: A four-week online program of short mindfulness and self-compassion exercises lowered daily stress and anxiety. Guided audio helped people calm the body's alarm system.
entries.source: Mind-OP online mindfulness and self-compassion program study
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Gratitude and mood
entries.content: Keeping a gratitude journal raised life satisfaction and lowered low mood in student and adult trials. Small and regular beats big and rare.
entries.source: Gratitude journaling intervention study; Emmons & McCullough (2003)
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Evening gratitude list
entries.content: Writing down things you're grateful for before bed for two weeks improved happiness and mood in a randomized trial. Giun's evening journal is built on this.
entries.source: Positive Psychology and Gratitude Interventions: A Randomized Clinical Trial - Frontiers
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Money stress and attention
entries.content: Dwelling on money worries raises stress, and low income itself is a real strain. Noticing small good moments each day can buffer some of that stress while you work on the practical side.
entries.source: Gratitude interventions RCT - Frontiers; Self-compassion writing RCT
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Better sleep with CBT-I
entries.content: CBT for insomnia beats simple relaxation for falling and staying asleep. It is the first treatment many sleep experts recommend.
entries.source: The Efficacy of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy: A Review of Meta-analyses - PMC
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Keep the bed for sleep
entries.content: 'Stimulus control' means using the bed only for sleep: phone out, get up if you can't sleep after a while. It retrains the brain to link bed with rest.
entries.source: CBT Techniques & Interventions - CBT Los Angeles
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Sleep and mood
entries.content: Short sleep makes emotions feel bigger and patience shorter the next day. A steady bedtime is one of the simplest mood tools.
entries.source: NIH NHLBI: Sleep deprivation and deficiency
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Plan small good things
entries.content: 'Activity scheduling' means putting small rewarding activities on your calendar instead of waiting for motivation. Doing them lifts mood and rebuilds routine.
entries.source: Mechanisms of change in CBT: implications for clinical practice
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Five-minute start
entries.content: Breaking a big task into tiny steps ('shaping') beats procrastination. Start with five focused minutes; early wins build momentum.
entries.source: CBT Techniques & Interventions - CBT Los Angeles
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Habits take about 66 days
entries.content: In a UCL study, new habits took 66 days on average to feel automatic (range 18 to 254). Missing a day didn't ruin progress.
entries.source: Lally et al. (2010), European Journal of Social Psychology
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Reframe early, don't bottle up
entries.content: Changing how you see a situation before the feeling peaks works better than pushing feelings down afterward. Suppression tends to backfire.
entries.source: Neuroscience of human social interactions and adult attachment style; emotion regulation research
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Stress is a signal
entries.content: Seeing stress as your body getting ready to act, rather than as harm, can improve how people perform under pressure.
entries.source: Jamieson et al. (2012), Journal of Experimental Psychology: General
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Personality science vs saju
entries.content: Psychologists measure personality with the Big Five (openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism). Birth charts are a cultural tradition and haven't been shown to predict personality.
entries.source: APA; Carlson (1985), Nature
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: When to talk to a professional
entries.content: If low mood, worry or anger lasts more than two weeks, gets in the way of work or relationships, or you feel unsafe, talk to a doctor or counselor. In a crisis call or text 988 (US).
entries.source: NIMH; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only
